+-- `{{#let}}`: bind the hash in a child frame whose context/loop-vars are the
+-- parent's (never re-roots), then render the body in it. The hash is the desugared
+-- `@hash` → `(dict …)` expression; `rt.letScope` builds the frame the same way the
+-- interpreter's `letH` does with `pushHelpers`.
+letBlock :: Rec -> Ctx -> Maybe Expr -> Template -> String
+letBlock rec ctx hash body =
+  let
+    child = rec.child ctx
+    hashJs = maybe "{}" (rec.expr ctx) hash
+  in
+    "  out += rt.letScope(" <> ctx.scope <> ", " <> hashJs <> ", " <> lambda rec child body <>
+      ");\n"
+

+-- | `let`: install the hash's `name → value` pairs as nullary operations in a
+-- | helpers-only frame, then render the body. Unlike `with`, the context, loop
+-- | variables, and reserved chain pass through **unchanged** (`pushHelpers`, not
+-- | `pushFrame`) — `let` never re-roots, it only aliases (ADR-024 §1). The MaxBars
+-- | surface `{{#let a=1 b=(add a 1)}}` desugars to *nested* single-binding lets, so
+-- | each `let` here carries one hash pair and the nesting gives left-to-right
+-- | sequential scope (`b` sees `a`) in a single walk. No `{{else}}` clause.
+letH :: forall m. MonadThrow Error m => Operation m (RefEnv m)
+letH ctl _ = case ctl.hash of
+  Just (VObject m) -> renderSafe ctl (pushHelpers (map constOperation m) ctl.env) (mainBody ctl)
+  _ -> renderMain ctl
+

 ### 1. Block-scoped `{{#let}}` — alias only, never re-root
 
+> *Implementation note (2026-06-08).* Shipped as specified — sequential, never re-rooting — with two
+> deviations from §5's sketch. (a) `let` is a **kernel block operation** (`Kernel.Prelude.letH`), *not* a
+> dedicated `Let` AST node: it reads its bindings from the surface hash and renders the body through the
+> context-preserving `pushHelpers` (the env stack already had it). The sequential semantics come from the
+> MaxBars desugar **nesting** multi-binding lets into single-binding ones — `{{#let a=1 b=(add a 1)}}` ⇒
+> `{{#let a=1}}{{#let b=(add a 1)}}…` — so an inner binding's value is evaluated in the frame the outer
+> installed (a single walk, no second pass). The compiled twin is `rt.letScope` (interpreter ≡ compiled,
+> `test:compile`). (b) The MaxBars-only scoping is enforced by **gating the desugar** to MaxBars; a
+> *FullBars* `{{#let}}` is currently inert (not rejected) — the §Gates `check:isolation` diagnostic is a
+> tracked follow-up.
+
 `{{#let}}` installs *nullary operations* at the block's lexical scope; they vanish at `{{/let}}`. It is
 the operation model applied to template-local *constants* — no new concept, just a new way to write one.

+## Let bindings
+
+`{{#let name=expr …}}…{{/let}}` ([ADR-024](/adr/adr-0024-let-and-dict-literal/))
+installs *block-scoped aliases* — template-local constants for a deep path, a
+computed value, a small lookup table — that vanish at `{{/let}}`. Each name is a
+nullary operation returning its value:
+
+```handlebars
+{{#let total=(add price tax) label="Subtotal"}}
+  {{label}}: {{total}}
+{{/let}}
+{{#let u=order.customer}}{{u.name}} — {{u.email}}{{/let}}
+```
+
+Two properties define it:
+
+* **Sequential.** Bindings evaluate left-to-right, each in the scope extended by
+  those to its left, so `{{#let a=1 b=(add a 1)}}` binds `b` to `2`. There is no
+  self- or forward-reference (a sequential `let`, not a `letrec`).
+* **Never re-roots.** Unlike `{{#with}}`, `let` only *aliases* — it does not shift
+  the context, so a bare `{{name}}` in the body still resolves against the current
+  context. `{{#let u=user}}{{name}}{{/let}}` reads the *root* `name`, not
+  `user.name` (write `{{u.name}}`). The complement holds:
+  `{{#with x as p}}` ≡ `{{#with x}}{{#let p=this}}…{{/let}}{{/with}}`.
+
+A binding whose name matches an in-scope operation shadows it for the body
+(`{{#let add="…"}}` reads the alias, not the `add` helper). Values are any
+expression — including a dict or list literal (`{{#let cfg={theme: "dark"}}}`).
+The surface desugars to nested single-binding lets, which the engine installs with
+`pushHelpers` (the context-preserving frame push); it is MaxBars-only sugar over
+that one engine primitive (FullBars stays Handlebars-faithful and uses
+`{{#with x as |n|}}` for aliasing).
+
